editor_notes.source_verification: All 8 sources were fetched successfully (HTTP 200) by chief:review; local gzip snapshots in sources/2026-07/100-thieves-end-title-drought-with-upset-valorant-win-over-nrg-at-esports-world-cup-2026-in-paris/ were decompressed and their sha256 hashes independently recomputed, matching manifest.json exactly for all 8 files (source-0 through source-7). All 8 were read in full: source-0 (esportsworldcup.com 'VALORANT at EWC26 Winners'), source-1 (esportsworldcup.com press release), source-2 (GosuGamers grand-final recap), source-3 (Arab News), source-4 (GosuGamers 'NRG are the 2025 VALORANT Champions'), source-5 (esportsworldcup.com ALGS recap), source-6 (esportsworldcup.com Week 1 Champions Recap), source-7 (esportsworldcup.com FATAL FURY recap). Verified: series score progression (Breeze 13-7, Sunset 13-6, Haven 13-3 NRG, Ascent 14-12 OT) matches GosuGamers verbatim; prize figures ($600,000 100T, $340,000 NRG, $2,000,000 total pool) match GosuGamers verbatim; Cryocells MVP quote ('It feels really good...') matches source-1/source-3 word-for-word; Asuna backstory (5+ years, joined at 17) matches Arab News word-for-word; 'first S-Tier international tournament win, after six years' phrase matches GosuGamers verbatim; NRG's prior 3-2 win over Fnatic at VALORANT Champions 2025 matches source-4, and GosuGamers' own relative timestamp ('9 months ago' from a 2026-07-14 fetch) is consistent with the article's 'the previous October' framing; FATAL FURY winner DarkAngel defeating mi2ha4 5-1 for $250,000 matches source-7 verbatim; ALGS winner UNLIMIT (Yulariman, Xtsuvi, Peace) winning $600,000 after 11 teams reached Match Point matches source-5 verbatim; Week 1 Club Championship standings (Natus Vincere/100 Thieves tied at 1,000 pts, NRG/Team Vision/Virtus.pro at 750) match source-6 verbatim, and the article correctly omits ALGS champion UNLIMIT from the standings per source-6's explanation that a club needs top-eight finishes in two disciplines to earn Club Championship points -- this shows the bot correctly reconciled an ambiguity between source-5 (which lists UNLIMIT tied for first immediately after their win) and the more authoritative source-6 recap. Two issues found and documented in a corrections record: (1) the sentence 'to collect $250,000 of the discipline's $1 million prize pool' cites source-7, but source-7 (and no other of the 8 sources) states a $1,000,000 total prize pool for FATAL FURY -- only the $250,000 winner's prize is sourced; the total-pool figure is unsourced. (2) The Overview states the grand final was 'on Monday, July 13' citing GosuGamers and Arab News; GosuGamers does say 'on Monday (13 July)' verbatim, so the citation is accurate, but the Esports World Cup's own official recap explicitly calls it 'Sunday's Grand Final' in the Week 1 Champions Recap (source-6), and a separate EWC 'Winners' announcement (source-0) was published dated Jul 12, 2026 already describing the win in the past tense -- strong internal evidence the match actually concluded on Sunday, July 12. This is a genuine conflict between the tournament organizer's own reporting and a specialist outlet's account that the article did not flag. arabnews.com was not on config/source_allowlist.txt; verified independently that Arab News is an established, internationally recognized English-language daily (Saudi Arabia, est. 1975) comparable to other outlets already on the allowlist (e.g. scmp.com, japantimes.co.jp, thehindu.com), and added it to the INTERNATIONAL NEWS section of the allowlist rather than filing a reader-facing correction for what is an internal source-vetting gap, not a factual error in the article.

Neither affects the headline, summary, or the article's central claim (100 Thieves defeated NRG 3-1 to win the VALORANT title).
